  "text": "The water climbed to Mara’s knees. Her father hauled her onto the steps, but the harbor master stayed at the gate, gripping the bars.

“Close it,” he said.

The key was still in the hidden lock. Mara’s father reached for it. From beyond the grate came three knocks, slow and deliberate.

The woman pushed past them. “That was our signal,” she said. “When he came home after dark.”

The figure lowered its hand. The light drifted aside, revealing a face Mara knew only from the photograph above the woman’s hearth: Elias, older now, with salt-white hair. He stood in water that did not seem to touch his coat.

“Don’t open it,” he said.

The harbor master let go of the bars.

Elias looked over his shoulder. The light swung with him, briefly showing shapes crowded along the channel. Mara could not tell whether they were people or the upright timbers of wrecked boats. Then one of them moved.

“I promised I’d come back,” Elias told the woman. “I didn’t promise I’d come alone.”

Her father turned the key. The gate shuddered, but the rising water held it open a finger’s width. Mara saw the red cloth in her hand and understood: it had caught in the hinge. She pulled hard. The scarf came free, and the gate slammed shut.

The bell stopped ringing. Water drained between the stones. When Mara looked up, the light and Elias were gone.

The woman took the scarf from her. Its torn end was dry. She folded it carefully and waited beside the gate until dawn."
